answer: The prover commits to a set inclusion proof over the registry of claimants, and the proof is small because it carries the exclusion of every competing holder, so two identities claiming the same resource would have to produce contradictory proofs. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. The copper is the unique resource, the lagoon the proof that excludes every other holder, and the zenith the registry that makes the exclusion checkable; cloning the copper forces two contradictory lagoon proofs, and the zenith is where the contradiction shows.
